summary.text: 今 means “now” or “today,” a temporal use attested in Shang oracle-bone writing. Early forms have a mouth-like upper shape and a lower mark, but what the graph depicts remains disputed.

formation.text: The early graph is commonly described by its visible parts: a mouth-like upper shape and a lower mark. Interpretations of the whole include a mouth-related sign and a wooden clapper; another proposal connects it with groaning or chanting and suggests the graph was reused for “now” because the words sounded alike. The object’s name and that proposed sound match are unknown, so this borrowing account remains unproven. In the later Shuowen analysis, 今 is divided into 亼 and 乁, with 乁 identified as an ancient form of 及; this dictionary analysis does not settle the early graph’s construction. Separately, 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟. That later sound role does not establish that groaning or chanting was the original word written by 今.

components.text: Early forms are described as a mouth-like upper shape above a lower mark, sometimes omitted. This is a proposed pictorial reading of the whole graph; the mark’s referent is disputed.
In the received dictionary analysis, 亼 is the first part of 今. This later division does not establish 亼’s role in the early graph.

The received analysis identifies the second part as 乁, an ancient form and variant of 及. This does not make 及 an ancestor of the shape in 今. Another transcription gives 绁; the intended shape and reason for the discrepancy remain unresolved.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms have a mouth-like upper shape and a lower horizontal mark, sometimes omitted. In seal-script forms, the lower mark bends downward. These graphic changes do not identify what the mark represents.

The received dictionary analysis divides 今 into 亼 and 乁, identifying the latter as an ancient form of 及. Another transcription renders the second part as 绁. This later analysis does not confirm the early graph’s construction.

uncertainties.text: The early graph’s referent and construction remain disputed. Mouth-related and wooden-clapper readings are proposals. Groaning or chanting is also proposed as an earlier word, but is not established as the word originally written by 今.

The name and pronunciation of an object proposed in the mouth-related or clapper readings are not established. The pronunciation of the temporal word 今 cannot supply that missing evidence, so a sound-based borrowing account remains unproven.
A possible connection between 今 and 其 (“this”) has been proposed, but neither a historical relationship nor a semantic path is established.
The cited oracle-bone example has no individual absolute date in the inspected account. It attests early temporal use but does not establish an earlier meaning or a sequence of semantic development.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone inscription; individual date unresolved
senses.text: The phrase 今夕其雨 attests the temporal meaning “now” or “today.” This is the earliest supported meaning, not proof of a hypothetical original meaning.
今 is also used for “present,” “current,” and “modern era,” but the examples available here do not date how these uses developed from the earlier temporal sense.
One proposal connects the graph with groaning or chanting, but this is not established as the word originally written by 今.

limitations.text: The Shang temporal attestation does not establish a prior sense or a sequence of semantic development. The listed modern meanings do not date when they arose.
The proposed connection to groaning or chanting does not establish that the graph was borrowed to write “now” or “today”; no donor-word pronunciation or sound match is independently established.

overview.text: 今 means “now” or “today,” attested in Shang oracle-bone writing. Early forms show a mouth-like upper shape over a lower mark that bends in seal script; what the graph depicts remains disputed.

components.text: Early forms show a mouth-like top over a lower mark; the mark bends in seal-script forms. Its referent remains disputed.
The later Shuowen analysis names 亼 as the first part of 今. Its relation to the early mouth-like upper shape remains uncertain.
The analysis identifies 乁 as a variant and ancient form of 及. This later account does not establish it as an original part of 今.

relationships.text: 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟. In the Zhengzhang system, 今 is reconstructed as krɯm and 吟 as ŋɡrɯm: their rhyme sequences are comparable, though their initials differ. This later role does not establish 今’s proposed original word.
